newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Raeford wins Laker Belgium/Holland cargo contract.
newsitem.headline: Raeford wins Laker Belgium/Holland cargo contract.

text.p: Raeford Aviation Services said it has recently started acting as Laker Airways' cargo general sales agent in the Netherlands and Belgium.
Laker operates DC-10 flights from London Gatwick to the U.S. To connect with these, cargo is being trucked from Brussels and Amsterdam to London, said Raeford director Steve Dando.

Raeford Aviation is also a cargo gsa for Simba Airlines, which is one of the airline's affected by Amsterdam Schiphol Airport's tightened regulations concerning Chapter 2 aircraft, which are noisier than modern generation planes.
From April 1, Chapter 2 aircraft are forbidden to land and take-off between 6pm to 8am.
Charges were also doubled for these aircraft. For take-off weights of up to 100 tonnes, the fines are 1200 Dutch guilders and for above 100 tonnes, they are 1800 guilders.
Kenya-based Simba Airlines already flies regularly to Ostend, as well as to Schiphol.
It is now possible that Simba will increase its services to Ostend or fly into a regional airport in the Netherlands, said Dando, but he stressed that no decision had yet been taken.
"Much of the traffic is perishable and it will depend on what is acceptable to the shippers and Simba Airlines itself", he said.
